title: Which AI Engine Should You Optimize For First?
metaTitle: Which AI Engine Should You Optimize For First?
metaDescription: Start with Google, then ChatGPT, and measure all five engines once to find your gaps. See how the engines differ and how to decide with your own data.
primaryKeyword: which ai engine should i optimize for first
shortAnswer: Start with Google, then ChatGPT. Google's index feeds AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini, so one body of SEO work covers three surfaces, and ChatGPT is the most-used chatbot in Pew's 2026 US survey. Before you commit further, ask all five engines the same buyer questions once. Move Perplexity or Claude up only if your own buyers or data point there.
intro: Teams facing five engines usually do one of two things: freeze while waiting for a definitive ranking, or spread thin effort across all of them and see nothing move. Both are avoidable. The decision is mostly about sequencing, because much of the work is shared. Below: our default order and the reasons for it, how the engines differ, what carries across, and how to replace our default with your own data.

sections.heading: Which AI engine should you optimize for first?
sections.body:
Google first, ChatGPT second, and the rest only when your own data says so. Google comes first because its [generative features sit on its core Search ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), so ordinary SEO work counts across AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini. ChatGPT is second because, in [Pew's February 2026 survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/chart/chatgpt-tops-the-list-of-chatbots-americans-use/), more US adults said they use it than any other chatbot.

Override that default with these rules:

- **Your buyers research on Google first** (local services, ecommerce, most consumer categories): stay on Google. You are defending a channel you already have.
- **Your buyers ask an assistant for a shortlist** ("best CRM for a 10-person agency"): move ChatGPT to the front.
- **Your buyers are analysts, developers or researchers who check sources:** test Perplexity early, because it is built around linked answers.
- **Your buyers already work inside Claude:** test Claude early, but note it is a smaller audience overall.

We hold one position firmly: do not pick Perplexity or Claude first on a hunch. Pew's chatbot survey did not include Perplexity, and we found no first-party usage figure for it when we checked, so an early bet needs evidence from your own buyers.

![A forest path winding through sunlit trees](https://images.pexels.com/photos/14266699/pexels-photo-14266699.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do the major AI engines differ?
sections.body:
They differ in what they retrieve from and in which crawler you control, not in what good content looks like. The table lists what each vendor documents, plus Pew Research Center's measure of how many US adults say they ever use the chatbot.

| Engine | What the vendor documents | First move | US adults who ever use it (Pew, Feb 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google AI Overviews and AI Mode | Built on Google's [core Search ranking and quality systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) | Normal SEO: indexed, snippet-eligible pages | Not asked (inside Search) |
| Gemini app | [Grounding](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-common-crawlers) with content from the Google Search index | Same Google work; think before blocking Google-Extended | 24% |
| ChatGPT | [OAI-SearchBot](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) surfaces sites in ChatGPT search | Allow OAI-SearchBot | 44% |
| Perplexity | [PerplexityBot](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) surfaces and links sites in results | Allow PerplexityBot; allowlist it in your firewall | Not asked |
| Claude | [Claude-SearchBot](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler) improves search result quality | Allow Claude-SearchBot | 6% |

One trade-off sits in the Gemini row: Google says the Google-Extended token governs both Gemini training and grounding in Gemini Apps, while not affecting Search inclusion. Blocking it to limit training can therefore limit grounding too.

Read the last column carefully. [Pew's survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/chart/chatgpt-tops-the-list-of-chatbots-americans-use/) asked whether adults "ever use" a chatbot, not which one they trust for a purchase. It tells you about reach, not about your buyers.

sections.heading: What foundation carries across engines?
sections.body:
Crawlable pages, direct answers, a clear description of your brand, and independent sources that repeat it. These cost the same whichever engine you target first, which is why the order matters less than most debates suggest. Google also says no special markup or AI-specific files are needed for [its AI features](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features).

Start with access, because it is the cheapest check. In AEOeye's crawler access study (October 2026, 384 sites), only 16 sites (4.2%) blocked OAI-SearchBot, 24 (6.2%) blocked Claude-SearchBot and 35 (9.1%) blocked PerplexityBot. In our SaaS group, 1 of 193 blocked any AI retrieval bot. Method and limits are on our [AI crawler directory](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory).

So your robots.txt is rarely the blocker; your CDN or firewall might be. [Perplexity's documentation](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) says a web application firewall may need explicit allowlisting. Check those logs before you write a word.

After access, the shared work is the same everywhere:

1. Put the direct answer first on each page that matters.
2. Describe your brand the same way on your site and everywhere else.
3. Earn mentions on the third-party pages engines read.

![Flat lay of a nautical chart with a compass, ruler and pencil](https://images.pexels.com/photos/31805295/pexels-photo-31805295.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How do you decide with data?
sections.body:
Run the same unbranded buyer questions through all five engines once, then compare where you are named with where your buyers actually ask. Start on the engine with the biggest gap and the most buyer overlap. A one-time pass is enough to set your order.

1. **Ask your buyers.** Add "which AI tools did you use while researching?" to demos and onboarding. Check analytics for referrals from chatgpt.com or perplexity.ai.
2. **Write 5-10 unbranded questions** such as "best [category] for [use case]".
3. **Ask each engine, several times.** Answers vary: in [SparkToro's study](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-ais-are-highly-inconsistent-when-recommending-brands-or-products-marketers-should-take-care-when-tracking-ai-visibility/), 600 volunteers ran 12 prompts across ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI, a combined 2,961 times, and for ChatGPT and Google's AI there was under a 1 in 100 chance of getting the same brand list in any two responses.
4. **Log whether you are named, in what position, and who is named instead.**
5. **Pick the largest gap** where your buyers are present, and fix that engine first.

![Hands holding a menu and choosing items at a cafe table with coffee and dessert](https://images.pexels.com/photos/4921403/pexels-photo-4921403.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

Position matters because answers are close to winner-take-most. In AEOeye's audit records (127 audits, 892 answers, June to September 2026), 71.4% of 147 ranked brand mentions were in first place. Being named at all is the hard part.

Do not use our numbers to rank the engines. The sample is self-selected, and per-engine counts are not comparable: the free audit ran on Claude only until mid-2026, so Claude has 509 answers against 74 each for Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI, on different brands and questions. Four engines have fewer than 10 mentions. The aggregates are in our [public benchmark file](/resources/aeoeye-recommendation-benchmark-2026-09.json) and explained on [AI brand recommendation measurement](/blog/ai-brand-recommendation-measurement).

AEOeye's [free audit](/) asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions and shows the real answers. The $29 full report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity across 10 questions. It is a point-in-time check, not a daily tracker; for ongoing monitoring, dedicated trackers fit better.

sections.heading: When should you move on to the next engine?
sections.body:
Move on when the first engine's basics are done and your logged gap has closed or stalled. Basics means crawl access confirmed, key pages answer-first, and brand facts consistent. Then re-run the same questions and take the next-largest gap.

Plan a re-check each quarter rather than weekly. Answers shift between runs, so one week's change is mostly noise; a quarter's trend is not. For the full metric set, see [measuring AI visibility](/blog/measuring-ai-visibility).

If your buyers split between two engines, the engine comparison matters more than the order. Our [Perplexity vs ChatGPT comparison](/compare/perplexity-vs-chatgpt-for-brand-visibility) shows how those two cite differently, and our [engine guide](/blog/best-ai-search-engines) covers all six major products.

keyTakeaways: Default order: Google first (one body of SEO work covers AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini), ChatGPT second, others when your own data says so.
Pew's February 2026 survey: 44% of US adults say they ever use ChatGPT, 24% Gemini, 6% Claude; Perplexity was not asked.
Crawl access is the cheapest first check, and rarely the blocker: 4.2% of 384 sites in our study blocked OAI-SearchBot.
Run the same buyer questions through all five engines once, several times each, because lists vary run to run.
Do not rank engines from our benchmark: its per-engine samples are unequal and self-selected.

faqs.q: Should I optimize for ChatGPT or Google first?
faqs.a: Google first for most companies, because its core Search systems underpin AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini, so one body of SEO work covers three surfaces. Put ChatGPT first if your buyers ask an assistant for vendor shortlists. Confirm with a one-time test of the same buyer questions in both.

faqs.q: Do I need to optimize for every AI engine separately?
faqs.a: Not at the start. Crawl access, answer-first pages, a consistent brand description and independent mentions help across engines. Engine-specific work is mostly crawler settings: OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT, PerplexityBot for Perplexity, Claude-SearchBot for Claude, and normal Google crawling for Google's features.

faqs.q: Which AI chatbot has the most users?
faqs.a: In Pew Research Center's February 2026 survey of US adults, 44% said they ever use ChatGPT, against 24% for Gemini, 17% for Copilot and 6% for Claude. Perplexity was not included. Google's AI Overviews sit inside Search, so Pew did not count them as a chatbot.

faqs.q: How often should I re-check which engine to prioritize?
faqs.a: Once a quarter is enough for most teams. Ask the same questions, several times each, and compare where you are named. Single runs are noisy, so look for a trend across a quarter, not a change from one week to the next.
